Issue: 564
Summary: OpENer commit 76b95cf has an out-of-bounds read in Connection Manager handling of malformed CIP ForwardOpen/LargeForwardOpen requests. `ForwardOpenRoutine()` in `source/src/cip/cipconnectionmanager.c` calls `ConnectionObjectInitializeFromMessage()` before strict minimal-length validation, and that parser in `source/src/cip/cipconnectionobject.c` repeatedly uses `GetByteFromMessage()`, `GetUintFromMessage()`, and `GetUdintFromMessage()` in `source/src/enet_encap/endianconv.c` without a remaining-readable-length parameter for per-read boundary checks. A valid ENIP frame carrying a malformed ForwardOpen or LargeForwardOpen with insufficient request data can therefore leave the input pointer at the end of the receive buffer and still make `GetByteFromMessage()` read past it. The supplied ASan run reports `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow` / `READ of size 1` in `GetByteFromMessage`, reached via `ConnectionObjectInitializeFromMessage()` and `ForwardOpenRoutine()`, overflowing the stack `incoming_message` buffer and aborting. The document states the issue is remotely triggerable over network traffic without authentication.
Reproduce: Prerequisites: the provided Python 3 PoC and an AddressSanitizer-instrumented POSIX OpENer binary from commit 76b95cf. Issue: 574
Summary: OpENer v2.3 / master branch up to commit `76b95cf` misparses `ForwardOpen` connection paths in `ParseConnectionPath()`. `CipEpathGetLogicalValue()` advances the `message` pointer according to the actual logical-segment encoding width, but `ParseConnectionPath()` decrements `remaining_path` by a fixed 1 word for the class segment and by 1 or 2 words based on the decoded value for configuration-instance and connection-point segments, instead of the segment’s actual on-wire width. When small values such as class `0x04`, configuration instance `151`, and connection points `150` and `100` are intentionally encoded as 32-bit logical segments, the parser consumes more path words than it accounts for, so `message` can move past the end of the received TCP packet while `remaining_path` remains positive. Issue: 577
Summary: OpENer v2.3 / master branch up to commit 76b95cf is reported vulnerable in the TCP explicit-messaging path (RegisterSession -> SendRRData). A crafted EtherNet/IP SendRRData request can reach the Connection Manager instance services ForwardClose (0x4E), GetConnectionData (0x56), or SearchConnectionData (0x57) and trigger a stack-buffer-overflow read. The report attributes this to missing minimum request-body length validation in these handlers after Message Router path decoding: a long but syntactically acceptable padded EPath can consume the remaining CIP payload, leave request_data_size == 0, and the handlers still call GetUintFromMessage() / GetUdintFromMessage() on message_router_request->data. The reported result is an out-of-bounds read past the stack receive buffer, with stated impact of at least remote unauthenticated denial of service.

[SOURCE id=issue:571:571-summary:fe57e1bf0770 kind=issue issue=571 path=distilled_issue/4.OpENer/#571.txt]
Issue: 571
Summary: In OpENer v2.3 / master branch up to commit `76b95cf`, `ParseConnectionPath()` in `source/src/cip/cipconnectionmanager.c` mishandles connection-path accounting during server-side `ForwardOpen` processing. The function tracks the path length in 16-bit words, but in the `kNetworkSegmentSubtypeProductionInhibitTimeInMilliseconds` branch it advances `message` by 2 bytes and subtracts `2` from `remaining_path`, even though that segment occupies only 2 bytes (1 word). When a crafted EtherNet/IP `ForwardOpen` places this Production Inhibit Time-in-milliseconds network segment as the last word of the connection path on a non-cyclic connection, `remaining_path` underflows from `1` to a very large `size_t` value. The parser then continues its `while (remaining_path > 0)` loop and calls `GetPathSegmentType()` on a pointer that has already advanced past the end of the received TCP message buffer. The documented observed result, with ASan/UBSan enabled, is a reproducible stack-based out-of-bounds read reported as `stack-buffer-overflow` / `READ of size 1` in `GetPathSegmentType()`.
Reproduce: Build and run the OpENer server with ASan/UBSan enabled, listening on EtherNet/IP TCP port 44818. Use the provided Python 3 PoC against that server; by default it targets `127.0.0.1:44818` and uses `crash` mode, or accepts `script.py [baseline|filler|crash] [host]`. In `crash` mode, the client: 1) opens a TCP connection to the server, 2) sends an EtherNet/IP `RegisterSession` request and reads the returned session handle, 3) builds a `SendRRData` packet carrying a CIP `ForwardOpen` request, 4) sets the connection path to the normal base path plus a 209-word simple data filler segment, then appends a trailing Production Inhibit Time in milliseconds network segment `0x43 0x01`
